AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise is structurally excellent — AWS reaccelerating to 28% YoY growth with a $364B backlog, advertising at 22%+ growth with 80%+ contribution margins, and new structural pillars in custom silicon ($20B ARR) and logistics monetization (ASCS). Q1 2026 results showed record 13.1% operating margin and $181.5B revenue (+17% YoY), with Q2 guidance of $194-199B above consensus. However, the stock is priced at 38.5x P/E — the top of its 365-day range — with a negative equity risk premium of -181bps vs the 10Y Treasury. The Q3 2025 operating margin trough of 9.7% (per quant pack) is partially offset by the Q1 2026 recovery to 13.1%, but the core tension remains: $220B in annual capex has compressed TTM FCF to $1.2B (95% decline), and the stock's rally of +21.8% in one quarter is predominantly multiple expansion rather than earnings growth. Oil at $98.38/bbl (+52%) is an unpriced logistics cost headwind. The franchise quality supports a positive lean, but the stretched valuation and capital-intensity risk cap the score well below strongly attractive territory. No dated near-term catalyst beyond the already-reported Q1 beat.
